audience: Casey's engineering manager and cross-functional partners
purpose: Explain verified movement, active attention, and the next decision for the week.

sections.title: Orientation
sections.summary: The week produced a measured reconciliation improvement while enterprise rollout remained ready behind one review dependency.

sections.title: Movement
sections.summary: Checkpoint batching improved the recorded replay, and the rollout plan moved to three support-sized cohorts.

sections.title: Attention
sections.summary: Security review is the active rollout dependency, and the first cohort needs a manager decision.

sections.title: Forward view
sections.summary: The next validation step is to test alert thresholds against replay spikes before paging is enabled.

claims.statement: Checkpoint batching reduced the recorded 50,000-record replay from 18 minutes to 6 minutes.
claims.implication: The measured reduction addresses the linked issue that replay exceeded the operations window.

claims.statement: The enterprise rollout will use three cohorts instead of one broad launch.
claims.implication: Each cohort stays within the response capacity of one on-call pair and retains a pause point.

claims.statement: The enterprise pilot is waiting on completion of the data-retention review.
claims.implication: Implementation is ready, but the first cohort cannot start until security completes the review.

claims.statement: The manager needs to choose the first cohort by Friday, August 28.
claims.implication: A Friday decision lets enablement send the onboarding schedule.

claims.statement: Next period, validate alert thresholds against replay spikes before enabling paging.
claims.implication: Threshold validation keeps synthetic replay behavior from creating noisy operational alerts.

claims.statement: Staging load tests use replay-safe mode so duplicate callbacks do not invalidate comparisons.
claims.implication: The operating detail explains how the replay benchmark remains comparable.
